bihar_raw_news.content: News On AIR | August 24, 2026 7:55 AM Bihar Government issues notification for formation of five-member committee for examination reforms Bihar Government has issued a notification for the formation of a five-member special committee to bring comprehensive reforms in the state’s examination system. The committee will be headed by a retired Supreme Court judge or a serving or retired High Court judge. The committee will submit its recommendations to the state government within three months. Its mandate will cover secondary and higher secondary, university, professional and technical, entrance and eligibility, as well as recruitment and competitive examinations. The committee will recommend measures to prevent question paper leaks, cheating, malpractice at examination centres, tampering with answer sheets and unauthorised interference in results. It will also focus on making the examination calendar, question paper security, evaluation and declaration of results more transparent and time-bound. The committee will review the use of digital technology, artificial intelligence, data analytics and cybersecurity measures in examinations. It will also recommend strengthening biometric verification, CCTV surveillance and secure tracking of question papers and answer sheets. Special attention will be given to safeguarding the interests of students from rural areas, economically weaker sections and those with limited access to digital facilities.

bihar_raw_news.title: " Bihar Govt committed to education of youth": CM Samrat Choudhary reaffirms Student ...
bihar_raw_news.content: "Bihar Govt committed to education of youth": CM Samrat Choudhary reaffirms Student Credit Card Scheme Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Monday reiterated that the Student Credit Card Scheme upto Rs 4 Lakh will remain available for higher education, reassuring students and parents across the state. ANI | Updated: 24-08-2026 13:49 IST | Created: 24-08-2026 13:49 IST Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary (File Photo/ANI). Image Credit: ANI Country: India SHARE Key Takeaways AI Summary Analyzing article... Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Monday reiterated that the Student Credit Card Scheme upto Rs 4 Lakh will remain available for higher education, reassuring students and parents across the state. This comes after the Bihar government said that reports claiming a reduction in education loans available to students under the Bihar Student Credit Card Scheme are incorrect. In an X post, CM Choudhary reaffirmed the state government's committment to ensuring better education for the youth. "There should be no doubt whatsoever in the minds of students and parents regarding the Student Credit Card Scheme. A Student Credit Card of up to ₹4 lakh is available for higher education, and this facility will continue to remain in place as before. The Bihar Government is fully committed to the education of youth and their bright future. Financial resources will never be allowed to become an obstacle in the path of education." The State government has further expanded the scope of financial assistance for students pursuing higher education, a release said. According to the Secretary of the Higher Education Department, an education loan of up to Rs 2 lakh will now be provided through the Bihar State Education Finance Corporation. Meanwhile, financial assistance ranging from Rs 2 lakh to Rs 4 lakh will be made available through scheduled commercial banks. Previously, the entire amount of up to Rs 4 lakh was provided solely through the Bihar State Education Finance Corporation. The objective of integrating the Bihar Student Credit Card Scheme with the Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan Yojana, the PM VidyaLakshmi Portal, and banks, according to the press release "is to provide institutional financial assistance for higher education to the maximum number of students." Additionally, students will be able to access education loans of up to Rs 10 lakh through the PM VidyaLakshmi Yojana. Thus, students now have more options for financial assistance for higher education compared to the past. An expenditure of Rs 886 crore was approved for the Bihar Student Credit Card Scheme in the 2025-26 financial year. For the current financial year (2026-27), an expenditure of Rs 950 crore has been approved. Consequently, the approved expenditure for the scheme in the current financial year is Rs 64 crore higher than in the previous financial year. (ANI) (This story has not been edited by Devdiscourse staff and is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.) POST / READ COMMENTS

bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary announces 'Mati Kala Board' in 3 months to promote Prajapati community, traditional pottery art ANI 23 Aug 2026, 23:31 GMT+10 Patna (Bihar) [India], August 23 (ANI): Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Chaudhary on Sunday announced that a Maati Kala Board (Terracotta Art Board) would be constituted within the next three months to preserve and promote the traditional art form and work for the welfare of the Kumhar (Prajapati) community. Choudhary made the announcement while addressing a programme organised by the Bihar Kumhar (Prajapati) Samanvay Samiti at Shri Krishna Memorial Hall in Patna to mark the death anniversary of Amar Shaheed Ramchandra Vidyarthi and felicitate newly elected members of the Bihar Legislative Council. The Chief Minister inaugurated the programme by lighting a ceremonial lamp and paying a floral tribute to Ramchandra Vidyarthi. Addressing the gathering, the Chief Minister, as per a Bihar CMO statement, said, 'I welcome you all to this programme organised by the Bihar Kumhar (Prajapati) Coordination Committee. On this occasion, I pay my heartfelt tributes to the immortal martyr Ramchandra Vidyarthi. At the age of just 13, the immortal martyr Ramchandra Vidyarthi sacrificed his life for the country's freedom. His life and sacrifice are a source of inspiration for us all. It is our collective responsibility to remember his contribution to the freedom struggle and to pass on his ideals to the new generation. Today is a day to remember three brave martyrs; I also pay my respects and offer tributes to Pandit Rajkumar Shukla and the immortal martyr Ramphal Mandal.' The Chief Minister stated, 'We are actively concerned about how the Prajapati community can move forward and progress.' He said the Prajapati community shapes even ordinary clay into the form of idols and, through its art, labour and skill, has enriched Bihar's culture and traditions for centuries.' He said everyone must work together to beautify Bihar and propel it forward by charting a new roadmap for its development. Two women from the Prajapati community, Sheila Pandit and Shivrani Prajapati, have been entrusted with responsibilities as Members of the Legislative Council (MLCs), according to the statement. The Chief Minister urged them to reach out to the people and do whatever is possible for the development of the community and to ensure justice for them. He said the government stood ready to support the community's advancement and the pursuit of justice wherever needed. The Chief Minister stated that Bihar's Mati Kala (clay art) is a vital part of the state's rich folk and traditional culture. A Mati Kala Board will be constituted within the next three months to preserve and promote this traditional art form, he said. He noted that the Board would work systematically for the welfare of the Kumhar (Prajapati) community and artisans associated with clay art. Initiatives will also be taken to provide artisans with modern technology and training, as well as ensure better marketing and market access for their products. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Government Forms Five-Member Panel to Address Examination Issues
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Government Forms Five-Member Panel to Address Examination Issues Bihar Education Header News Published By - Hency Thacker August 24, 2026 Reading time - 2 min. Facebook X Copy URL WhatsApp The Bihar government has established a five-member expert committee aimed at recommending substantial reforms in the state’s examination framework. This initiative seeks to enhance the security, transparency, fairness, and effectiveness of examinations across various educational institutions and recruitment agencies. The notification regarding the committee’s formation was released by the General Administration Department on August 23. The committee’s mandate includes a comprehensive review of the examination procedures administered by state examination boards, commissions, and universities, as well as recruitment agencies. It will assess all aspects of the examination process—from candidate registration to question paper preparation, examination conduct, evaluation, result declaration, grievance resolution, and record keeping. The government has identified increasing complexity in the examination system, stemming from a growing number of candidates, the expansion of higher education options, intensified competition for government roles, and the adoption of digital technologies and artificial intelligence, necessitating these reforms. Focus on Preventing Malpractices A crucial area of scrutiny for the committee is the prevention of various forms of malpractice. This includes question paper leaks, impersonation, cheating, and tampering with answer sheets and examination results. The panel will also investigate security measures and protocols surrounding examination data to mitigate potential breaches.

bihar_raw_news.title: "Will review air connectivity, NH projects, preserving Bihar's heritage": JDU's Sanjay Jha on ...
bihar_raw_news.content: "Will review air connectivity, NH projects, preserving Bihar's heritage": JDU's Sanjay Jha on Parliamentary panel's visit ANI | Updated: Aug 24, 2026 09:55 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Bihar ( Patna ) [India], August 24 (ANI): Chairperson of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture and Janata Dal (United) leader Sanjay Jha said on Monday that the committee's visit to Bihar will focus on strengthening air and road connectivity, preserving the state's cultural heritage and developing tourism infrastructure. Speaking about the committee's three-day visit to Bihar, Jha said discussions will be held on the expansion of airports and air connectivity, including the international greenfield airport announced in the Union Budget, as well as national highway and road projects in the state. "There will be a complete discussion related to aviation. There will be a discussion on NH and road-related projects in Bihar, like Patna -Purnia, Gorakhpur-Siliguri and other projects like NH-27 , which are not in good condition," Jha told ANI. He said the committee will also review issues related to Bihar's art and cultural heritage, including the upkeep of museums, the Khuda Bakhsh Library and historical sites under the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI). "There will be a discussion on culture. We are going to the Bihar Museum and Khuda Bakhsh Library . There are many historical sites of ASI which are not well maintained, like Kumrahar. There will be a discussion on that," he said. The committee will travel to Gaya on Monday evening, where a meeting on tourism will be held on Tuesday. Jha said discussions will cover the development of major tourist destinations, including Bodh Gaya and Rajgir , as well as projects announced in the Union Budget. "Tourism is a very big sector for Bihar. We believe that if tourism succeeds, it becomes a very big sector for employment," Jha said. He said the committee's recommendations will be submitted to Parliament, following which the concerned departments will take further action. "When a committee comes, all the officers stay. So there is a detailed discussion. And then the timeline of other things is decided. The committee's report is submitted to Parliament. And then the department follows it up on the basis of this report," he said. Jha said the committee's visit was important for reviewing centrally funded projects and giving further momentum to development of transport connectivity, tourism and culture in Bihar. The committee will also visit Bihar Museum in Patna and later conduct on-site inspections of Bodh Gaya , Rajgir and Nalanda . (ANI)

national_raw_news.content: External Affairs Minister Dr S. Jaishankar called on Russian President Vladimir Putin at Kremlin today. Indian Ambassador to Russia Vinay Kumar and Joint Secretary (ERS) Mayank Singh were also part of the delegation. The two leaders discussed ways to strengthen India-Russia ties and expand cooperation across key sectors. The meeting focused on bilateral trade, economic cooperation, and preparations for upcoming high-level summits. Speaking at the meeting, Dr S Jaishankar highlighted the strong and growing India-Russia partnership, particularly in the areas of economic cooperation, trade and energy. He conveyed Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s greetings and handed over a personal message from Mr Modi. Dr Jaishankar said, the two sides held a meeting of the Intergovernmental Commission earlier in the day and described the outcome as positive. He said, ties between India and Russia have grown significantly across several sectors, including trade, energy, fertilizers and nuclear cooperation. The External Affairs Minister also said Prime Minister Narendra Modi looks forward to meeting the Russian President at the SCO Summit in Bishkek and welcoming him to India for the BRICS Summit. He added that the two leaders are expected to hold their annual summit at a mutually convenient time. Dr Jaishankar said the developments reflect a strong picture of cooperation between India and Russia. Speaking during a meeting, Russian President Putin offered to increase fertilizer supplies to India, saying Moscow is taking steps to support Indian farmers and the country’s agricultural sector. He also highlighted the growth in trade between Russia and India this year. He said the two countries are cooperating in practically all areas, reflecting the broad and expanding nature of their bilateral partnership. Earlier in the day, External Affairs Minister along with Russian First Deputy Prime Minister Denis Manturov co-chaired a meeting of the India-Russia Inter-Governmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific, Technological and Cultural Cooperation in Moscow. Speaking at an event, Dr Jaishankar said, the India-Russia partnership has consistently demonstrated resilience and adaptability. He said, even amid a complex international landscape, bilateral engagement has continued to deepen, reflecting the mutual interests and confidence that underpin the partnership. The Minister highlighted key areas that need to be addressed to achieve the 100-billion-dollar bilateral trade target by 2030, including progress on market access, the removal of tariff and non-tariff barriers, strengthening payment mechanisms, and greater business-to-business engagement. During the meeting, the two sides discussed ways to further expand bilateral trade and economic cooperation and reviewed the India-Russia partnership. Dr Jaishankar reached Moscow yesterday on a two-day visit to Russia. During his visit, the External Affairs Minister is also scheduled to meet his Russian counterpart Sergey Lavrov to exchange views on regional and global issues.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | National 28 India and China to discuss boundary issues during NSA Ajit Doval’s visit to Beijing
national_raw_news.content: National Security Advisor Ajit Doval arrived in Beijing today on a two-day visit to China. During his visit, Mr Doval will take part in the 25th round of Special Representatives talks between the two countries on the boundary issue with his Chinese counterpart and Foreign Minister Wang Yi scheduled to be held in Beijing tomorrow. Announcing the Special Representatives talks at a media briefing today, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said, Mr Doval and Mr Wang will have an in-depth discussion on the boundary issue as well as other bilateral, regional and international relations. The ties between New Delhi and Beijing came under severe strain after the 2020 Galwan Valley clash and the prolonged military stand-off in eastern Ladakh. But both sides have since taken steps to stabilise relations. Mr Doval and Mr Wang are the designated Special Representatives for the boundary talks mechanism, which was established in 2003 to comprehensively address the boundary dispute of the India-China border spanning over three thousand four hundred kilometers. Ahead of Special Representatives talks in Beijing, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar on Saturday reiterated that peace and tranquillity along the border areas are a prerequisite for good relations with China. During his visit, the National Security Advisor will call on China’s Vice President Han Zheng.

According to a report by The Times of India cited by Odisha TV, AAI has submitted the proposal to the Union Finance Ministry’s Public Investment Board (PIB). If approved, the project will pave the way for the tendering process. The proposed terminal is aimed at meeting the airport’s growing passenger demand and is planned to bring domestic and international flight operations under one roof. New terminal to handle 8.6 million passengers The proposed Terminal 3 is expected to have an annual passenger-handling capacity of 8.6 million. At present, BPIA operates two separate terminals. Terminal 1 handles domestic flights, while Terminal 2 caters to international operations, including customs and immigration facilities. The new terminal is expected to streamline these operations and offer an integrated experience for passengers travelling on both domestic and international routes. Land available within airport premises Officials said land for the proposed T3 is available within the airport’s operational area, near the existing Terminal 1 building. The final design will be prepared after taking into account factors such as air traffic growth, passenger convenience and commercial activities, officials said. The airport currently has 18 aircraft aprons leading to the bays. Once the proposed Terminal 3 becomes operational, the airport is expected to require six additional aerobridges. How Bhubaneswar airport expanded over the years Biju Patnaik International Airport originally operated with a single terminal, which served domestic passengers. The old domestic terminal was subsequently converted into the international terminal, T2, in March 2013. A new domestic terminal was later constructed at a cost of ₹145 crore. Built on a modular design, the existing Terminal 1 was planned to allow further expansion and can handle around 1,000 passengers during peak periods. With passenger traffic expected to grow further, the proposed Terminal 3 could significantly expand the airport’s capacity while integrating domestic and international operations. What happens next? The immediate step is the Public Investment Board’s approval of the proposal. Once the required approval is secured, AAI can proceed with the tendering process for the project.
